column1: What is the SC-300 module on Microsoft Entra tenant configuration covering?
column2: Company branding, Microsoft Entra roles, delegation via administrative units, custom domains, evaluating permissions, and tenant-wide settings.

column1: What prerequisite experience is assumed for this module?
column2: Prior usage experience with the Azure portal UI or the Microsoft Entra admin center.

column1: Which license is required to configure custom company branding on sign-in pages?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID Premium P1, P2, or Office 365 (for Office 365 apps).

column1: Where in the portal do you configure company branding?
column2: Azure portal > Microsoft Entra ID > Manage menu > Company branding. (The menu option only appears with a premium license.)

column1: Which branding setting is automatically set as the default and cannot be changed?
column2: The language.

column1: What are the size and file-size limits for the sign-in page background image?
column2: Max 1920x1080 pixels and max file size 300,000 bytes; only .png or .jpg supported.

column1: What is the maximum length of the username hint text, and what format must it use?
column2: Max 64 characters, must be Unicode, no links or code. (Not recommended if guests sign in.)

column1: What is the maximum character limit for sign-in page text and formatting?
column2: 1,024 characters; must be Unicode.

column1: Where does the banner logo appear?
column2: On the sign-in page after the user enters a username, and on the My Apps portal page.

column1: Microsoft Entra roles vs Azure roles — what do they manage?
column2: Azure roles control permissions to manage Azure resources; Microsoft Entra roles control permissions to manage Microsoft Entra resources.

column1: What is the scope of a Microsoft Entra role?
column2: Tenant level, or it can be applied to an Administrative Unit.

column1: What is the scope of an Azure role?
column2: Multiple levels: management group, subscription, resource group, or resource.

column1: What role does the person who signs up for the Microsoft Entra tenant become?
column2: The first Global Administrator.

column1: What happens when a Global Administrator elevates access via the "Access management for Azure resources" switch in the Azure portal?
column2: They are granted the User Access Administrator (Azure) role on all subscriptions for that tenant.

column1: What can the User Access Administrator role do?
column2: Grant other users access to Azure resources (useful to regain access to a subscription).

column1: Does the Global Administrator have access to Azure resources by default?
column2: No. But Global and User Administrator roles do span Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365 (e.g., Exchange, SharePoint).

column1: Which role can reset the password for any user and all other administrators?
column2: Global Administrator.

column1: What can the User Administrator role manage?
column2: Create/manage users and groups, manage support tickets, monitor service health, change passwords for users, Helpdesk admins, and other User Administrators.

column1: What can the Billing Administrator role do?
column2: Make purchases, manage subscriptions, manage support tickets, monitor service health.

column1: Where can you see the list of Microsoft Entra roles in the Azure portal?
column2: On the "Roles and administrators" screen.

column1: List four ways to assign Microsoft Entra roles.
column2: To a user/group via Roles and administrators; via Users/Groups > Assigned roles; via Access control (IAM) at broad scopes (subscription, resource group, management group); via PowerShell/Microsoft Graph or PIM.

column1: Which experience is used for all role management tasks if you have Microsoft Entra ID P2 and use PIM?
column2: Privileged Identity Management (PIM) — note you can only assign one role at a time.

column1: At what scopes can a custom Microsoft Entra role be assigned?
column2: Directory-level scope or app registration resource scope only.

column1: What portal path creates a custom role?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID > Roles and administrators > New custom role (Basics > Permissions > Review + create).

column1: What is Microsoft's recommendation about the Global Administrator role?
column2: Avoid using it; follow the principle of least privilege.

column1: In the exercise, which license trial is activated to complete exercises requiring PIM?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID Premium P2 (via Licenses > Get a free trial).

column1: How do you assign a role to a user through the user's profile?
column2: Users > All Users > select user > Assigned roles > Add assignments > select role > Add.

column1: What is an administrative unit in Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: A container for other Microsoft Entra resources — it can contain only users, groups, and devices.

column1: What problem do administrative units solve?
column2: They restrict permissions in a role to a portion of the organization, enabling least-privilege delegation (e.g., a User Administrator managing only one region/department).

column1: Which five admin roles can manage an administrative unit?
column2: Authentication administrator, Helpdesk administrator, License administrator, Password administrator, User administrator.

column1: Which on-premises Active Directory concept is comparable to administrative units?
column2: Organizational Units (OUs).

column1: What are the three expected stages of administrative unit adoption in an organization?
column2: Initial adoption, pruning, stabilization.

column1: Application Administrator vs Cloud Application Administrator — key difference?
column2: Cloud Application Administrator has all Application Administrator abilities except Application Proxy settings (no on-premises permission).

column1: What does the Application Administrator role NOT grant?
column2: The ability to manage Conditional Access.

column1: How do you selectively grant users the ability to register applications?
column2: Set "Users can register applications" to No in User settings, then assign users to the Application Developer role.

column1: What happens when an Application Developer creates a new application registration?
column2: They are automatically added as the first owner of the application.

column1: What can the Enterprise Application Owner role manage?
column2: The enterprise apps they own (SSO settings, user/group assignments, adding owners) — but not Application Proxy settings or Conditional Access.

column1: What can the Application Registration Owner role manage?
column2: App registrations they own, including the application manifest and adding other owners.

column1: What does Security Defaults enforce on privileged Microsoft Entra accounts?
column2: Multifactor authentication (available at no extra cost to all organizations).

column1: Name one default permission difference between member users and guest users.
column2: Members can enumerate the list of users and their contacts and register new applications; guests cannot (guests can only read their own properties and search non-hidden groups by name).

column1: In User settings, which user abilities can you restrict?
column2: Registering applications, accessing the Azure portal, LinkedIn connections, and settings for external collaboration.

column1: Where can you view the full list of permissions granted by a role?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID > Roles and administrators > select role > description page via the ellipsis (...) menu.

column1: Which role grants non-admins read access to basic directory information via the admin portal?
column2: Directory Readers.

column1: Does restricting access to the Microsoft Entra administration portal block PowerShell or Visual Studio access?
column2: No — it only restricts the administration portal, not PowerShell or other clients.

column1: Who can manage domains in Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: Only a Global Administrator.

column1: What is the initial domain name when a tenant is created, and what is its role?
column2: E.g., contoso.onmicrosoft.com — it is also the primary domain name (default for new users).

column1: What is the limit on managed domain names per organization? And if all domains are federated?
column2: Up to 900 managed domain names; up to 450 domain names if configuring all for federation with on-premises AD.

column1: What must you do before adding a subdomain like europe.contoso.com?
column2: Add and verify the root domain (contoso.com) first; the subdomain is then automatically verified.

column1: Can a subdomain of a domain owned by another tenant be verified in a different tenant?
column2: Yes — you'll be prompted to add a TXT record at the DNS hosting provider.

column1: Name three conditions that prevent deleting a custom domain name.
column2: A user has a username/email/proxy address with the domain; a group has an email/proxy address with it; an app has an app ID URI that includes it.

column1: What does ForceDelete do to references to the custom domain?
column2: Renames UPN, EmailAddress, ProxyAddress (users), group EmailAddress, and application identifierUris to the initial default domain (e.g., user@contoso.onmicrosoft.com) via an asynchronous operation.

column1: What are the requirements/limits for using ForceDelete?
column2: Fewer than 1000 references to the domain; Exchange-provisioned references (mail-enabled security groups, distribution lists) must be updated/removed in the Exchange Admin Center first.

column1: When does ForceDelete return an error?
column2: If the number of objects to rename is greater than 1000, or if one of the applications is a multitenant app. (Also fails if the domain was purchased via Microsoft 365 domain subscription services or if you're a partner administering on behalf of another customer.)

column1: Does changing the DNS registrar for a custom domain require configuration changes in Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: No additional configuration tasks; the domain continues to work without interruption.

column1: Where is the tenant display name configured?
column2: Microsoft Entra admin center > Identity > Overview > Properties > Name.

column1: Which tenant property cannot be changed after the tenant is created?
column2: Country or region.

column1: Who does Microsoft contact if there's a data breach and no Global privacy contact is listed?
column2: The administrator who owns the tenant.

column1: What four protections are provided by Security Defaults?
column2: MFA registration for all users, MFA for administrators, blocking legacy authentication protocols, and MFA when necessary / protecting privileged activities like Azure portal access.

column1: Which Conditional Access policy equivalent of Security Defaults requires Microsoft Entra ID Premium P2?
column2: Require MFA registration (requires Identity Protection, part of P2).

column1: Which external collaboration setting controls who can invite guests?
column2: Guest invite settings (from guests themselves to only admins).

column1: What are the three ways Microsoft Entra ID typically defines users?
column2: Cloud identities, directory-synchronized identities, and guest users.

column1: What is the "Source" value of a directory-synchronized user in Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: Windows Server AD.

column1: What is the "Source" value of a guest user account?
column2: Invited user.

column1: What is the recommended synchronization tool for most organizations syncing on-premises AD to Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync — lightweight cloud-managed agent, supports multiple disconnected forests.

column1: When should you use Microsoft Entra Connect Sync instead of Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync?
column2: For complex scenarios such as device synchronization or groups with more than 50,000 members.

column1: You need to switch between directories in the Microsoft Entra admin center. Which panel do you use?
column2: The Directory + Subscription panel (or the Switch directory button in the toolbar).

column1: What happens to a cloud identity user when the account is removed from the primary directory?
column2: It is deleted.

column1: Which admin center is used to work with user objects in Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: The Microsoft Entra admin center.

column1: What does Microsoft Entra ID build after a user is authenticated to determine resource access?
column2: An access token.

column1: How long does a deleted user account remain in a suspended (restorable) state?
column2: 30 days; after that, permanent deletion starts automatically.

column1: Which roles can restore or permanently delete users?
column2: Global administrator, Partner Tier-1 Support, Partner Tier-2 Support, or User administrator.

column1: You deleted a user 45 days ago and need to restore the account. What is the outcome?
column2: Restoration is impossible — after the 30-day window, permanent deletion has started and a permanently deleted user cannot be restored.

column1: Where in the Microsoft Entra admin center do you restore a deleted user?
column2: Identity > Users > Deleted users > select user > Restore user.

column1: What are the two group types in Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: Security groups and Microsoft 365 groups.

column1: Which members can a security group contain?
column2: Users, devices, and service principals.

column1: What do Microsoft 365 groups provide that security groups do not?
column2: Collaboration features — shared mailbox, calendar, files, SharePoint site — and access for people outside the organization.

column1: Which group type is available to end users (not just admins) to create?
column2: Microsoft 365 groups; security groups require a Microsoft Entra administrator.

column1: What are the three group membership types?
column2: Assigned, Dynamic User, and Dynamic Device.

column1: Can Microsoft 365 groups use dynamic device membership?
column2: No — Dynamic Device applies to security groups only; Microsoft 365 groups support dynamic users but not dynamic devices.

column1: What license is required for dynamic group membership?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID P1 (or Intune for Education for device-based rules).

column1: A user's department attribute changes from Sales to Marketing. What happens to dynamic membership rules?
column2: All dynamic membership rules in the tenant are re-evaluated, and the user is added to or removed from groups accordingly.

column1: What is the primary audience for Microsoft Entra registered devices?
column2: Bring your own device (BYOD) and mobile device scenarios using personal devices.

column1: How do users sign in to a Microsoft Entra registered device?
column2: With a local account (e.g., a Microsoft account), with a Microsoft Entra account attached for access to organizational resources.

column1: How do users sign in to a Microsoft Entra joined device?
column2: With an organizational Microsoft Entra account.

column1: Microsoft Entra registered vs Microsoft Entra joined — which requires an organizational account to sign in to the device?
column2: Microsoft Entra joined; registered devices only require a local credential with the Entra account attached.

column1: Which Windows editions are excluded from Microsoft Entra join?
column2: Home editions.

column1: What are the three methods to deploy Microsoft Entra joined devices?
column2: Out of Box Experience (OOBE), bulk enrollment, or Windows Autopilot.

column1: What defines a hybrid Microsoft Entra joined device?
column2: A device joined to on-premises Active Directory and registered with Microsoft Entra ID.

column1: You have Win32 apps relying on AD machine authentication and want to keep using Group Policy. Which device option should you use?
column2: Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices.

column1: What replaced device writeback for hybrid identity scenarios?
column2: Cloud Kerberos Trust — allows Entra joined and hybrid joined devices to authenticate to on-premises resources without device objects written back to AD.

column1: Which MDM tool is used to enforce configurations like storage encryption and password complexity on registered devices?
column2: Microsoft Intune (Mobile Device Management).

column1: Which licenses enable group-based licensing?
column2: Paid or trial Microsoft Entra ID Premium P1 or greater, or paid/trial Office 365 Enterprise E3 or greater.

column1: You have 1,000 unique members in licensed groups. How many licenses must you have?
column2: At least 1,000 — one license for each unique member of licensed groups.

column1: Where is group-based licensing managed?
column2: Only through the Microsoft 365 admin center (Billing > Licenses > Groups).

column1: A user is assigned the same license both directly and via a group. How many licenses are consumed?
column2: Only one — the license is consumed once.

column1: What happens to users without a specified usage location during group license assignment?
column2: They inherit the usage location of the directory.

column1: Which PowerShell cmdlet is used to assign licenses to a user?
column2: Set-MgUserLicense.

column1: PowerShell error "CountViolation" indicates which group licensing problem?
column2: Not enough licenses available for the product.

column1: PowerShell error "MutuallyExclusiveViolation" indicates which problem?
column2: Conflicting service plans — two service plans that cannot be assigned to the same user.

column1: PowerShell error "DependencyViolation" indicates which problem?
column2: Other products depend on the license — a service plan required by another service plan is being removed.

column1: PowerShell error "ProhibitedInUsageLocationViolation" indicates which problem?
column2: The user's usage location isn't allowed for the service being assigned.

column1: Example: user has Office 365 E1 directly assigned; you add them to a group with E3. Assignment fails. Why?
column2: Conflicting service plans — e.g., SharePoint Online Plan 2 conflicts with Plan 1, Exchange Online Plan 2 conflicts with Plan 1.

column1: Does Microsoft Entra ID automatically resolve license conflicts?
column2: No — the decision about how to resolve conflicting product licenses always belongs to the administrator.

column1: What exception appears in audit logs when the same license is concurrently assigned to a user via multiple groups?
column2: LicenseAssignmentAttributeConcurrencyException — Entra ID retries automatically; no customer action required.

column1: What must you do before deleting a licensed group?
column2: Remove all licenses assigned to the group.

column1: When a licensed group is deleted and a user has a dependent license (e.g., Audio Conferencing), what happens to the group-assigned license?
column2: It is converted from inherited to a direct license assignment.

column1: Microsoft Workplace Analytics requires which prerequisite service plan?
column2: Exchange Online (Plan 1) or Exchange Online (Plan 2).

column1: How do you manually reprocess a group or user to resolve license errors?
column2: Open Licenses on the group or user pane and select the Reprocess button on the toolbar.

column1: During migration to group-based licensing, why should you keep direct assignments until group licenses are verified?
column2: To avoid users temporarily losing licenses; when the same license is assigned directly and via group, only one license is consumed.

column1: What message confirms group license processing has completed?
column2: Latest license changes have been applied to all users.

column1: What are custom security attributes in Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: Business-specific key-value pairs you can define and assign to Microsoft Entra objects for storing information, categorizing objects, or fine-grained access control.

column1: Which data types do custom security attributes support?
column2: Boolean, integer, and string — with single or multiple values, free-form or predefined values.

column1: Which objects can custom security attributes be assigned to?
column2: Microsoft Entra users and enterprise applications (service principals).

column1: Are custom security attributes supported in SAML token claims or JWT claims?
column2: No — they are not supported in Microsoft Entra Domain Services, SAML token claims, or JWT claims.

column1: What does SCIM stand for?
column2: System for Cross-Domain Identity Management — an open standard protocol for automating exchange of user identity information between identity domains and IT systems.

column1: Which SCIM version does the Microsoft Entra Provisioning Service use?
column2: SCIM 2.0.

column1: What is an HCM system in the SCIM provisioning context?
column2: A Human Capital Management system that automates HR processes throughout the employee lifecycle (the source of user data).

column1: What is API-driven inbound provisioning used for?
column2: For HR systems without a SCIM endpoint — any automation tool or script can send workforce data to the Microsoft Entra provisioning API (GA March 2024).

column1: Name supported authoritative sources for API-driven inbound provisioning.
column2: Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, and any custom HR system integrated via the API.

column1: What is Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration?
column2: A feature of Microsoft Entra External Identities that lets you invite external users (guests) to access your apps and resources with their own credentials, while you keep control of corporate data.

column1: How can you identify a B2B collaboration user object in the directory?
column2: UserType is typically "Guest" and the user principal name contains the #EXT# extension.

column1: Who can invite guest users by default?
column2: All users in the tenant, including guests, can invite guest users — even without an admin role.

column1: Which role can be assigned to delegate guest invitations to non-admin users?
column2: The Guest Inviter role.

column1: What can guest users see in the directory by default?
column2: They cannot list users, groups, or other directory resources, but they can see membership of non-hidden groups.

column1: Which guest user access setting is the most restrictive?
column2: Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects — guests can only view their own profile.

column1: What is the portal path to configure external collaboration settings?
column2: Microsoft Entra admin center > Identity > External Identities > External collaboration settings.

column1: Can you create both an allowlist and a blocklist for collaboration restrictions?
column2: No — you can create only one type of list, and only one policy per organization.

column1: What is the maximum size of the collaboration restrictions policy?
column2: 25 KB (25,000 characters), including the allow/blocklist and any other configured parameters.

column1: Do B2B invitations expire?
column2: No — an invitation of a user does not expire.

column1: What must a guest user do after being invited to access resources?
column2: Redeem the invitation, via the redemption URL in the invitation email or a direct link to the shared app.

column1: How do you invite many guest users at once?
column2: Identity > Users > All users > Bulk operations > Bulk invite; download the CSV template, fill it in, upload, then verify.

column1: Which rows of the bulk invite CSV template must never be removed or modified?
column2: The first two rows: the version number row and the column headings row.

column1: What must you do with the examples row in the bulk CSV template?
column2: Remove it and replace it with your own entries.

column1: Which email addresses are not supported for guest invitations?
column2: Group email addresses; plus (+) addressing is also not supported — omit the + and any text after it up to the @.

column1: What are the required values in the bulk invite CSV?
column2: Email address to invite [inviteeEmail] and the redirection URL the user is forwarded to after accepting the invitation.

column1: What does the UserType property indicate?
column2: The user's relationship to the host tenant: Member (employee) or Guest (external collaborator). It has no relation to sign-in method or directory role.

column1: Can a B2B collaboration user have UserType = Member?
column2: Yes — change it in the Microsoft Entra user properties, e.g., when the partner belongs to a larger parent organization.

column1: What does an Identities value of "mail" mean for a guest user?
column2: The user signed up using Microsoft Entra Email one-time passcode (OTP).

column1: What does an Identities value of google.com or facebook.com mean?
column2: The user signed up via self-service with a Gmail or Facebook account.

column1: What is recommended for granting B2B/guest users privileged roles?
column2: Follow least privilege and use Privileged Identity Management (PIM) to grant access.

column1: Which Microsoft 365 external collaboration activity is disabled by default?
column2: Shared channel in Teams (it uses an existing Microsoft 365 external account).

column1: Which Microsoft 365 external collaboration settings are enabled by default?
column2: Authenticated file/folder sharing, site sharing, team sharing, external chat and meetings, anonymous meeting join, and unauthenticated file/folder sharing.

column1: Which license is required to create and use dynamic groups?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID Premium P1 or P2.

column1: Which dynamic membership rule includes all users, both members and guests?
column2: user.objectId -ne null (Membership type: Dynamic User).

column1: What is Microsoft Entra Verified ID?
column2: A decentralized identity service to issue and verify verifiable credentials; verifiers get a free REST API to request and accept credentials in apps.

column1: What are the prerequisites to deploy Microsoft Entra Verified ID?
column2: An Azure tenant with a subscription, a Microsoft Entra ID premium license, signed in as global administrator, and a configured Azure Key Vault.

column1: What is the purpose of the Domain setting in Verified ID setup?
column2: It binds your DID to your domain; wallets use it to validate the DID and display a verified symbol.

column1: What is the current name for direct federation?
column2: SAML/WS-Fed identity provider (IdP) federation.

column1: Which protocols must a partner IdP support for SAML/WS-Fed IdP federation?
column2: SAML 2.0 or WS-Federation (WS-Fed).

column1: Does setting up SAML/WS-Fed federation change authentication for guests who already redeemed invitations?
column2: No — they keep their previous authentication method; only new guest users use the federated IdP.

column1: What happens to guest users if you delete a SAML/WS-Fed federation?
column2: They can no longer sign in; you can update their authentication method by resetting their redemption status.

column1: Which NameID format is required in the SAML 2.0 token?
column2: urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent

column1: Which WS-Fed identity providers have been tested for compatibility with Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: AD FS and Shibboleth.

column1: Google federation is designed for which users, and what should you use for G Suite domains?
column2: Gmail users (gmail.com/googlemail.com); for G Suite domains use SAML/WS-Fed (direct) federation.

column1: A Google guest user gets a "header too long" error. What is the fix?
column2: Clear cookies or open a private/incognito window and try to sign in again.

column1: Can users redeem invitations with Facebook accounts?
column2: No — Facebook works only for self-service sign-up user flows, not for invitation redemption.

column1: What must be enabled before adding Facebook as an identity provider?
column2: Self-service sign-up for the tenant; then set up a user flow and select Facebook as a sign-in option.

column1: What happens if you delete Google federation?
column2: Google guests who already redeemed their invitation cannot sign in; restore access by deleting them from the directory and reinviting them.

column1: What are the default cross-tenant access settings?
column2: B2B collaboration with other Microsoft Entra organizations is enabled; B2B direct connect is blocked.

column1: Inbound vs outbound access settings — what does each control?
column2: Inbound controls external users accessing your resources; outbound controls your users accessing external organizations' resources.

column1: What do inbound trust settings allow?
column2: Your Conditional Access policies can trust the external organization's MFA, compliant device, or hybrid Microsoft Entra joined device.

column1: What is B2B direct connect and where does it work today?
column2: A mutual trust between two Microsoft Entra organizations for seamless SSO; currently works with Teams shared channels.

column1: What is required to establish B2B direct connect?
column2: Both organizations must mutually enable B2B direct connect in their cross-tenant access settings.

column1: Which settings connect your tenant to Microsoft Azure Government or Microsoft Azure China?
column2: Microsoft cloud settings in cross-tenant access settings.

column1: What is hybrid identity?
column2: An identity solution spanning on-premises and cloud environments, providing unified authentication and authorization to resources regardless of their location.

column1: What is Microsoft Entra Connect and what are its five capabilities?
column2: The Microsoft tool that bridges on-premises AD with Microsoft Entra ID. Capabilities: synchronization, password hash synchronization (PHS), pass-through authentication (PTA), federation integration, and health monitoring.

column1: How many PTA agents are recommended for high availability?
column2: Three lightweight agents: the first on the Microsoft Entra Connect server plus two extra agents, so authentication continues if one agent is down for maintenance.

column1: You need to deploy PTA agents. Can you place them in a perimeter network (DMZ)?
column2: No. Agents must access on-premises AD DS including domain controllers and need outbound internet access, so perimeter network deployment is not supported.

column1: PTA agents cannot validate credentials due to a major on-premises failure. What is the fallback and how is it activated?
column2: Password hash synchronization can serve as a backup authentication method. Failover is not automatic — you must manually switch the sign-in method using Microsoft Entra Connect.

column1: Which sign-in scenarios require federated authentication instead of cloud authentication?
column2: Requirements Entra ID doesn't support natively: smartcard/certificate authentication, on-premises or third-party MFA servers, third-party authentication solutions, or sign-in with sAMAccountName (DOMAIN\username).

column1: Why should you enable PHS even when using PTA or federation?
column2: Three reasons: high availability/disaster recovery (cloud service scales globally), on-premises outage survival, and Identity Protection leaked-credentials detection (requires Entra ID P2).

column1: What is sourceAnchor (also called immutableId)?
column2: An attribute immutable during the lifetime of an object that uniquely identifies it as the same object on-premises and in Microsoft Entra ID; used for hard match and federation claims.

column1: What are the length rules for a sourceAnchor value?
column2: Fewer than 60 characters; characters other than a-z, A-Z, or 0-9 are encoded and counted as three characters each.

column1: Which sourceAnchor attribute should you use in a single-forest environment?
column2: objectGUID — also the attribute used by Express settings and DirSync.

column1: A user's UPN suffix (contoso.com) is not a verified domain in Microsoft Entra ID. What happens during sync?
column2: Microsoft Entra Connect replaces the UPN suffix with the default tenant domain, e.g., contoso.onmicrosoft.com.

column1: What is a Microsoft Entra Connect server in staging mode?
column2: A second server that reads data from all connected directories but writes nothing to them; it runs the normal sync cycle and serves as an updated standby.

column1: What is the maximum group size supported by Microsoft Entra Connect cloud sync, and which filter is recommended for large groups?
column2: Groups with up to 50,000 members; use only the OU scoping filter when synchronizing large groups.

column1: What exactly does PHS synchronize from on-premises AD?
column2: A hash of the hash of the user's password — Entra Connect extracts the AD password hash and applies extra security processing before synchronizing it to Microsoft Entra ID.

column1: How often does the PHS process run, and can you change this?
column2: Every 2 minutes; the frequency cannot be modified. Passwords sync more frequently than the standard directory synchronization window.

column1: Which Microsoft Entra Connect installation option enables PHS automatically?
column2: Express Settings. With custom settings, PHS is available on the User Sign-In page.

column1: PHS fails on a FIPS-locked-down server. What is the cause and fix?
column2: FIPS disables MD5. Fix: in miiserver.exe.config (under %programfiles%\Azure AD Sync\Bin), add `<enforceFIPSPolicy enabled="false"/>` under configuration/runtime.

column1: How does PTA validate passwords?
column2: A software agent on one or more on-premises servers validates passwords directly against on-premises Active Directory — password validation does not happen in the cloud.

column1: How do you enable pass-through authentication?
column2: Through Microsoft Entra Connect: choose PTA on the User Sign-In page during custom installation, or use the "Change user sign-in" task on an existing installation.

column1: Is PTA a per-domain or tenant-level feature?
column2: Tenant-level — enabling it affects sign-in for users across all managed domains in the tenant.

column1: When switching from AD FS to PTA, how long should you wait before shutting down AD FS, and why?
column2: At least 12 hours, to ensure users can keep signing in to Exchange ActiveSync during the transition.

column1: Which sign-in methods can seamless SSO be combined with?
column2: Password hash synchronization or pass-through authentication. Seamless SSO is not applicable to AD FS.

column1: In the seamless SSO browser flow, which account does the browser request a Kerberos ticket for?
column2: The AZUREADSSOACC computer account, which represents Microsoft Entra ID; Entra ID decrypts the ticket using a previously shared key.

column1: How can seamless SSO be rolled out, and does it require extra on-premises components?
column2: Rolled out to some or all users using Group Policy; no additional on-premises components are needed.

column1: What is federation?
column2: A collection of domains that have established trust — typically including authentication and almost always authorization — for shared access to a set of resources.

column1: What is the minimum AD FS version supported for federation with Microsoft Entra Connect?
column2: Windows Server 2012 R2 or later (new or existing farm).

column1: Where is the Web Application Proxy server deployed in an AD FS federation, and what is its role?
column2: In the perimeter network facing the extranet; it supports authentication requests coming from the extranet.

column1: Which two service account types can the AD FS service use?
column2: A group managed service account or a domain user account.

column1: What is device writeback used for?
column2: Enabling device-based conditional access for AD FS-protected devices by synchronizing devices registered in Entra ID back to on-premises AD (e.g., creating the CN=RegisteredDevices container).

column1: Where do you view sync error reports, and how often are they refreshed?
column2: In the Azure portal as part of Microsoft Entra Connect Health for sync; reports update every 30 minutes with errors from the latest synchronization attempt.

column1: Hard match vs soft match in Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: Hard match: incoming object's sourceAnchor matches a cloud object's immutableId. Soft match: fallback using ProxyAddresses and UserPrincipalName when no hard match is found (target must have no immutableId).

column1: What causes the InvalidSoftMatch sync error?
column2: The hard match fails and the soft match finds an object whose immutableId differs from the incoming object's sourceAnchor — typically two objects sharing a ProxyAddresses or UPN value.

column1: What causes the ObjectTypeMismatch sync error?
column2: Two objects of different object types (e.g., a user and a mail-enabled security group) share the same ProxyAddresses value, which Microsoft Entra ID does not allow.

column1: What causes the AttributeValueMustBeUnique sync error?
column2: Entra Connect tries to add or update an object with a ProxyAddresses or UserPrincipalName value already assigned to another object in Microsoft Entra ID.

column1: Which attributes typically trigger the LargeObject error, and what is the certificate hard limit?
column2: userCertificate, userSMIMECertificate, thumbnailPhoto, and proxyAddresses; the hard limit is 15 certificates.

column1: What causes the FederatedDomainChangeError sync error?
column2: A synchronized user's UPN suffix is changed from one federated domain to another federated domain (e.g., bob@contoso.com to bob@fabrikam.com), so the UPN doesn't update.

column1: An on-premises user cannot soft-match a cloud object that has an admin role assigned. How do you fix it?
column2: Remove the cloud account from all admin roles, hard-delete the quarantined object, let the next sync soft-match the users, then restore the role memberships.

column1: Which license is required to use Microsoft Entra Connect Health?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID Premium P1.

column1: Which role is required to register the Microsoft Entra Connect Health agent?
column2: Global administrator in Microsoft Entra ID — by default, the global admin account has permissions to register the agent.

column1: Which firewall ports must the Health agent be able to use?
column2: TCP 443 and TCP 5671. The latest agent version requires only port 443.

column1: Which Health agent is installed automatically?
column2: The Microsoft Entra Connect Health agent for Sync — installed automatically with the latest version of Microsoft Entra Connect.

column1: Where should you NOT install the Health agent for AD FS?
column2: On the Microsoft Entra Connect (Sync) server — the AD FS server must be a different machine with a unique host name.

column1: What happens when you delete a server from the Microsoft Entra Connect Health service?
column2: Data collection and monitoring stop for that server; the agent is not uninstalled and collected data isn't deleted (Azure retention policy applies). To re-monitor, uninstall and reinstall the agent.

column1: Which built-in Azure RBAC roles does Microsoft Entra Connect Health support?
column2: Owner (manage access, view all information, change settings), Contributor (view all information, change settings), Reader (view all information only). Other roles have no impact.

column1: Which RBAC role is required to use the Diagnose and Remediate feature for duplicated attribute sync errors?
column2: Contributor permission from Azure RBAC.

column1: What is hybrid identity?
column2: An identity solution spanning on-premises and cloud environments, providing unified authentication and authorization to resources regardless of location.

column1: You need to implement a hybrid identity solution. Which two tools are central to this?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Entra Connect.

column1: Which synchronization-related tasks are covered in the hybrid identity module?
column2: Plan/design/implement Microsoft Entra Connect, manage PHS and PTA, seamless SSO, federation (excluding manual AD FS deployments), troubleshoot sync errors, and implement Microsoft Entra Connect Health.

column1: What are the five capabilities of Microsoft Entra Connect?
column2: Synchronization, password hash synchronization (PHS), pass-through authentication (PTA), federation integration, and health monitoring.

column1: Which two sign-in methods fall under "cloud authentication" in a hybrid identity design?
column2: Password hash synchronization (PHS) and pass-through authentication (PTA).

column1: How often does the password hash synchronization process run as part of the Microsoft Entra Connect sync process?
column2: Every 2 minutes (frequency cannot be modified).

column1: You need to enforce on-premises account states, password policies, and sign-in hours immediately at sign-in time. Which authentication method should you use?
column2: Pass-through authentication (PTA).

column1: How many PTA agents are recommended for high availability?
column2: Three agents (one on the Microsoft Entra Connect server plus two extra).

column1: Can PTA agents be deployed in a perimeter network?
column2: No — agents need access to on-premises domain controllers and outbound internet access, so perimeter network deployment is not supported.

column1: What is the backup authentication method for PTA when agents can't validate credentials, and is failover automatic?
column2: Password hash synchronization; failover is NOT automatic — you must manually switch the sign-in method using Microsoft Entra Connect.

column1: Which authentication method is required for smartcard authentication, third-party MFA servers, or sign-in using sAMAccountName (DOMAIN\username)?
column2: Federated authentication (e.g., AD FS).

column1: Why should you enable password hash synchronization regardless of the chosen authentication method?
column2: For high availability/disaster recovery, on-premises outage survival, and Identity Protection (leaked credentials detection requires Entra ID Premium P2).

column1: What is the recommended way to protect against Microsoft Entra Connect server failure?
column2: Deploy a second Microsoft Entra Connect server in staging mode as a standby.

column1: What does a Microsoft Entra Connect server in staging mode do?
column2: It reads data from all connected directories and runs the normal sync cycle, but writes nothing to connected directories.

column1: What is the sourceAnchor attribute also called, and what is its definition?
column2: immutableId — an attribute immutable during the lifetime of an object that uniquely identifies an object as the same on-premises and in Microsoft Entra ID.

column1: Which attribute should be used as sourceAnchor for a single forest, and which is used with express settings?
column2: objectGuid.

column1: What are the length and character rules for the sourceAnchor value?
column2: Fewer than 60 characters; special characters are not allowed; must be globally unique; string, integer, or binary; not case-sensitive; shouldn't be based on the user's name.

column1: Which attribute does Microsoft Entra ID use to authenticate users, and what must its suffix match?
column2: userPrincipalName (UPN); the suffix must match a verified custom domain in Microsoft Entra ID.

column1: The UPN suffix contoso.com is not a verified domain in Microsoft Entra ID. What happens when users sync?
column2: The tool replaces the UPN suffix with the default domain, e.g., contoso.onmicrosoft.com.

column1: You run a non-routable domain like contoso.local. Which installation type does Microsoft Entra Connect suggest, and why?
column2: Custom settings — so you can specify the attribute to use as UPN for sign-in to Azure.

column1: What is the most common supported topology for Microsoft Entra Connect?
column2: Single on-premises forest (one or multiple domains) with a single Microsoft Entra tenant — the only topology supported by express installation.

column1: How many Microsoft Entra Connect sync servers are needed per Microsoft Entra tenant?
column2: One — there is a 1:1 relationship between a sync server and a tenant.

column1: What are the four staging areas/components Microsoft Entra Connect uses for synchronization?
column2: Connector Space (CS), Metaverse (MV), sync rules, and run profiles.

column1: How many Metaverses (MV) exist in a Microsoft Entra Connect deployment?
column2: Only one.

column1: What is Microsoft Entra Connect cloud sync, and what agent does it use?
column2: A synchronization solution for users, groups, and contacts to Microsoft Entra ID using the cloud provisioning agent, with sync configuration managed in the cloud.

column1: What is the maximum group member size supported by Microsoft Entra Connect cloud sync?
column2: 50,000 members (use only the OU scoping filter for large groups).

column1: Which scenario is cloud sync designed for regarding disconnected forests?
column2: Synchronizing to a Microsoft Entra tenant from multi-forest disconnected AD environments, e.g., mergers and acquisitions.

column1: What exactly does Microsoft Entra Connect synchronize for PHS?
column2: A hash of the hash of the user's on-premises AD password to Microsoft Entra ID.

column1: Can you revert a password hash to plain text?
column2: No — a hash is the result of a one-way mathematical function and cannot be reverted.

column1: During the first PHS enablement, can you define a subset of users to synchronize?
column2: No — the initial sync covers all in-scope users; selective password hash sync can be set up only after initial synchronization.

column1: Which installation option automatically enables PHS?
column2: Express Settings during Microsoft Entra Connect installation.

column1: On a FIPS-locked-down server, how do you enable MD5 for PHS?
column2: Edit miiserver.exe.config in %programfiles%\Azure AD Sync\Bin and add `<enforceFIPSPolicy enabled="false"/>` under the runtime node.

column1: Which federation product other than AD FS can be configured with Microsoft Entra Connect, and what is its minimum version?
column2: PingFederate, version 8.4 or later.

column1: How does PTA validate user passwords?
column2: A software agent on on-premises servers validates passwords directly against on-premises Active Directory — validation doesn't happen in the cloud.

column1: Through which tool do you enable pass-through authentication?
column2: Microsoft Entra Connect (custom installation path, or the "Change user sign-in" task on an existing install).

column1: Is PTA a tenant-level or per-user feature?
column2: Tenant-level — enabling it affects sign-in for users across all managed domains in the tenant.

column1: When switching from AD FS to PTA, how long should you wait before shutting down the AD FS infrastructure?
column2: At least 12 hours, to ensure users can keep signing in to Exchange ActiveSync during the transition.

column1: Which sign-in methods can be combined with seamless SSO, and which cannot?
column2: Works with PHS and PTA; NOT applicable to Active Directory Federation Services (ADFS).

column1: Which computer account in Active Directory represents Microsoft Entra ID for seamless SSO Kerberos tickets?
column2: AZUREADSSOACC.

column1: In browser-based seamless SSO, what HTTP response does Microsoft Entra ID use to challenge the browser for a Kerberos ticket?
column2: A 401 Unauthorized response, via JavaScript in the background.

column1: In seamless SSO, what does Microsoft Entra ID use to decrypt the Kerberos ticket?
column2: The previously shared key (the AZUREADSSOACC computer account's secret).

column1: What token does Microsoft Entra ID issue to a native client app after validating the Kerberos ticket in seamless SSO?
column2: A SAML token, which the app submits to the Microsoft Entra ID OAuth2 token endpoint to receive access, refresh, and ID tokens.

column1: What is the minimum Windows Server version for an AD FS farm used with Microsoft Entra Connect federation?
column2: Windows Server 2012 R2 or later.

column1: Where is the Web Application Proxy (WAP) server deployed in a federation topology?
column2: In the perimeter network, facing the extranet, to support authentication requests from the extranet.

column1: Do AD FS servers need to be domain-joined before federation setup? What about WAP servers?
column2: AD FS servers must be joined to Active Directory; domain join is not required for Web Application Proxy servers.

column1: Which two types of service accounts can the AD FS service use?
column2: Group managed service account or domain user account.

column1: How many domains can you federate during the initial Microsoft Entra Connect installation?
column2: Only a single domain; more domains can be added later by running Microsoft Entra Connect again.

column1: What is AlternateID sign-in used for in federation?
column2: Allowing users to sign in with an attribute other than UPN (e.g., mail) when the on-premises UPN uses a non-routable domain or can't be changed.

column1: What is device writeback used for?
column2: To enable device-based conditional access for AD FS-protected devices by synchronizing devices registered in Azure back to on-premises Active Directory.

column1: Where is the Synchronization Errors report available?
column2: In the Azure portal as part of Microsoft Entra Connect Health for sync.

column1: What are the three operation types Microsoft Entra Connect performs on directories?
column2: Import, Synchronization, and Export.

column1: What is a "Hard Match" in Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: Matching an incoming object's sourceAnchor attribute to the immutableId attribute of objects in Microsoft Entra ID.

column1: What is a "Soft Match" and which attributes does it use?
column2: A fallback match when hard match fails, using ProxyAddresses and UserPrincipalName attributes to match objects already present in Microsoft Entra ID.

column1: What causes an InvalidSoftMatch error?
column2: Hard match finds no object, but soft match finds an object that has a different immutableId value than the incoming object's sourceAnchor.

column1: Which attributes must have unique values in the Microsoft Entra directory schema?
column2: ProxyAddresses, UserPrincipalName, onPremisesSecurityIdentifier, and ObjectId.

column1: What does the Microsoft Entra Attribute Duplicate Attribute Resiliency feature do?
column2: It reduces sync errors by handling duplicated ProxyAddresses and UserPrincipalName more resiliently, allowing new objects to be provisioned — but it doesn't fix the duplicate data itself.

column1: What causes an ObjectTypeMismatch error?
column2: Two objects of different types (User, Group, Contact) have the same value for attributes used in soft match, e.g., the same ProxyAddresses value.

column1: What causes an AttributeValueMustBeUnique error?
column2: Microsoft Entra Connect tries to add/update an object with a ProxyAddresses or UserPrincipalName value already assigned to another object in Microsoft Entra ID.

column1: What causes an IdentityDataValidationFailed error?
column2: The UserPrincipalName attribute contains invalid/unsupported characters or doesn't follow the required format.

column1: What causes a FederatedDomainChangeError?
column2: A synchronized user's UPN suffix is changed from one federated domain to another federated domain (e.g., bob@contoso.com to bob@fabrikam.com).

column1: Which attributes typically trigger a LargeObject (ExceededAllowedLength) sync error?
column2: userCertificate, userSMIMECertificate, thumbnailPhoto, and proxyAddresses.

column1: What is the hard limit for certificates in the userCertificate and userSMIMECertificate attributes?
column2: 15 certificates.

column1: What causes an "Existing Admin Role Conflict" sync error?
column2: An on-premises user object with administrative permissions and the same UPN as an existing Microsoft Entra object — soft-matching is not allowed with cloud objects holding admin roles.

column1: How do you fix an Existing Admin Role Conflict?
column2: Remove the cloud account from all admin roles, hard delete the quarantined cloud object, let the next sync cycle soft-match, then restore the role memberships.

column1: How often are sync error reports in Microsoft Entra Connect Health for sync updated?
column2: Every 30 minutes, including errors from the latest synchronization attempt.

column1: What does Microsoft Entra Connect Health provide?
column2: Monitoring of on-premises identity infrastructure — alerts, performance monitoring, and usage analytics via the Microsoft Entra Connect Health portal.

column1: Which license is required to use Microsoft Entra Connect Health?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID Premium P1.

column1: Which administrative role is required to install and configure the Microsoft Entra Connect Health agent?
column2: Global administrator in Microsoft Entra ID.

column1: Which firewall ports must be open for the Microsoft Entra Connect Health agent?
column2: TCP 443 and TCP 5671 — the latest agent version requires only port 443.

column1: Which PowerShell version is required for the Health agent, and what must be disabled (FIPS)?
column2: PowerShell 4.0 or newer; FIPS (Federal Information Processing Standard) must be disabled.

column1: Should the AD FS Health agent be installed on the Sync server?
column2: No — the AD FS server should be different from the Sync server; don't install the AD FS agent on the Sync server.

column1: How is the Microsoft Entra Connect Health agent for Sync installed?
column2: It is installed automatically with the latest version of Microsoft Entra Connect.

column1: Which services verify the Health agent installation for AD FS and for Sync?
column2: AD FS: Diagnostics, Insights, and Monitoring Services. Sync: Sync Insights Service and Sync Monitoring Service.

column1: Are Microsoft Entra Connect Health email notifications enabled by default?
column2: Yes. Email notifications are enabled by default and are sent when an alert is generated and when it's resolved.

column1: Where in the portal do you configure email notifications for a Connect Health service?
column2: Open the Alerts dialog for the service, select Notification Settings in the action bar, set the switch to ON, then select Save.

column1: How can you make all global administrators receive Connect Health alert emails?
column2: In Notification Settings, select the check box to have all global administrators receive email notifications.

column1: How do you add extra recipients to Connect Health alert emails?
column2: Enter the addresses in the Additional Email Recipients box; to remove one, select the entry and select Delete. Save to apply.

column1: When do notification setting changes take effect in Connect Health?
column2: Only after you select Save. Changes take effect only after saving.

column1: How does Connect Health report back-end sync processing errors by email?
column2: Instead of one message per error, it sends a daily digest of all errors to the tenant's administrative contact email address(es).

column1: Which license is required for the steps to delete a server or service instance from Connect Health?
column2: A Microsoft Entra ID premium license is required for the deletion steps.

column1: What happens to monitoring when you delete a server from Connect Health?
column2: Data collection stops and the server is removed from monitoring — no new alerts, monitoring, or usage analytics data for that server.

column1: Does deleting a server in Connect Health uninstall the Health Agent?
column2: No. The agent is not uninstalled; if it remains installed, you may see Health Agent-related errors on the server.

column1: What happens to data already collected from a deleted server?
column2: It is not deleted immediately; it is deleted in accordance with the Azure data retention policy.

column1: What must you do to start monitoring the same server again after deleting it from Connect Health?
column2: Uninstall and reinstall the Health Agent on that server.

column1: What must you do to resume monitoring after deleting an entire service instance?
column2: Uninstall and reinstall the Health Agent on all the servers that were part of that service instance.

column1: How do you delete a server monitored by Connect Health for AD FS or Entra Connect (Sync)?
column2: Open the Server screen from the Server List, select Delete, type the server name in the confirmation box, then select Delete.

column1: How do you delete a domain controller monitored by Connect Health for Microsoft Entra Domain Services?
column2: Open the Domain Controllers dashboard, select the DC, select Delete Selected, confirm, then select Delete.

column1: How do you delete a service instance from Connect Health?
column2: Open the Service screen from the Service List by service identifier (farm name), select Delete, type the service name (e.g., sts.contoso.com), then select Delete.

column1: Which built-in Azure RBAC roles does Microsoft Entra Connect Health support?
column2: Owner, Contributor, and Reader. Other roles (e.g., User Access Administrator, DevTest Labs Users) have no impact on access.

column1: You need a user to view alerts and change settings (e.g., email notifications) but NOT manage access. Which role?
column2: Contributor — can view all information and change settings, but not manage access.

column1: What can an Owner do in Connect Health that a Contributor cannot?
column2: Manage access — e.g., assign a role to a user or group. Owners can also view all information and change settings.

column1: What can a Reader do in Connect Health?
column2: Only view all information (e.g., view alerts) from the portal.

column1: Who is assigned the Owner role in Connect Health by default, and can this be changed?
column2: Microsoft Entra global administrators are Owners by default; this assignment can't be changed.

column1: What are the two access scopes for managing Connect Health access?
column2: All service instances (recommended in most cases) and an individual service instance.

column1: A user has access at both the directory level and a service instance level. Is permission granted?
column2: Yes. Permission is granted if the user has access at either the directory or the service instance level.

column1: Is the Invite Users feature supported within Microsoft Entra Connect Health?
column2: No. The Invite Users feature isn't supported.

column1: You must grant a user Connect Health access across all monitored role types. What scope and path?
column2: All service instances scope: open the main Connect Health screen, then Configure > Users > Add, select the role, and add the user or group.

column1: Which sync error names indicate duplicated attribute conflicts?
column2: QuarantinedAttributeValueMustBeUnique and AttributeValueMustBeUnique.

column1: Which attribute conflicts are commonly seen with these sync errors?
column2: UserPrincipalName or Proxy Addresses conflicts; conflicting objects are quarantined in Microsoft Entra ID.

column1: Which duplicated attributes does the Connect Health diagnose feature support?
column2: UserPrincipalName and ProxyAddresses (both error types); SipProxyAddress and OnPremiseSecurityIdentifier (AttributeValueMustBeUnique only).

column1: Which Azure RBAC permission is required to use the diagnose feature for sync errors?
column2: Contributor permission from Azure RBAC.

column1: Is any upgrade or configuration required to enable the Connect Health diagnosis feature?
column2: No. No upgrade or configuration is required.

column1: What is the "orphaned object" scenario?
column2: The on-premises source object was deleted but the deletion never synced to Microsoft Entra ID; the existing user loses the Source Anchor, so a restored/recreated object can't match it.

column1: A cloud-only user exists in Microsoft Entra ID and a newly synced duplicate appears. Why can't they be matched?
column2: The objects have different Source Anchors and there is no direct way to remap the Source Anchor.

column1: What does the Diagnose status "Not Started" mean?
column2: The diagnosis process hasn't been visited; there may be a potential way to fix the sync error directly from the portal.

column1: What does the Diagnose status "Manual Fix Required" mean?
column2: The error doesn't fit portal fix criteria (e.g., conflicting objects aren't users) or diagnostics found no portal fix — on-premises fixes are still an option.

column1: What does the Diagnose status "Pending Sync" mean?
column2: A fix was applied and the portal is waiting for the next sync cycle to clear the error.

column1: Which button applies the portal-side fix for an identified orphaned object case?
column2: Apply Fix — the status changes to Pending sync and the error is removed after the next sync cycle.

column1: Diagnostics end with a Close button instead of a fix. What does this mean?
column2: No quick fix is available from the portal; use the shown on-premises solution. The error status switches to Manual fix required.

column1: Two users both have Joe.J@contoso.com as UPN and are quarantined. How can you fix it?
column2: Update the conflicting source object from the on-premises side; the sync error resolves after the next sync.

column1: Which sign-in/authentication options does the module cover for Microsoft Entra Connect?
column2: Password hash synchronization (PHS), pass-through authentication (PTA), Seamless single sign-on (Seamless SSO), and federation (excluding manual AD FS deployments).

column1: Beyond hybrid deployment, which management areas does the module cover?
column2: Managing Microsoft Entra Connect, managing PHS/PTA/Seamless SSO/federation, troubleshooting synchronization errors, and implementing/managing Microsoft Entra Connect Health.

column1: What is Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication?
column2: A security feature that requires two or more authentication elements for full authentication, limiting the impact of password exposure.

column1: What are the three categories of authentication elements used in MFA?
column2: Something you know (password, security answer), something you possess (mobile app, token device), something you are (biometric, e.g., fingerprint or face scan).

column1: A hacker obtained a valid username and password via social engineering. Which feature stops the sign-in?
column2: Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication — the password is useless without also possessing the second factor (trusted device, fingerprint, or face).

column1: Which Microsoft Entra feature locks out attackers brute-forcing passwords while treating valid-user sign-ins differently?
column2: Microsoft Entra smart lockout.

column1: Which Microsoft Entra feature blocks commonly used and compromised passwords using a global banned-password list?
column2: Microsoft Entra password protection.

column1: Which feature lets you configure risk-based policies that automatically block risky behaviors or require a password change?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID Protection.

column1: Which Microsoft Entra feature provisions security-enhanced remote access to on-premises web applications?
column2: Microsoft Entra application proxy.

column1: Which tool creates and manages a single identity per user across a hybrid enterprise, keeping users, groups, and devices in sync?
column2: Microsoft Entra Connect.

column1: Which offerings include Microsoft Entra MFA using security defaults?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2, Microsoft 365 Business, Microsoft Entra ID Free, and standalone Microsoft 365 licenses.

column1: Why is the layered approach of MFA effective?
column2: Even if a hacker learns the password, it's useless without the trusted device; a found device is useless without the password.

column1: How should you roll out an MFA deployment across an organization?
column2: In waves — start with a small pilot group to find setup issues and unsupported apps/devices, then broaden until fully enrolled.

column1: What resources does Microsoft provide to help draft MFA rollout communications?
column2: Communication templates, including posters and email templates.

column1: How is Microsoft Entra MFA enforced?
column2: With Conditional Access policies, which are IF-THEN statements (IF a user accesses a resource, THEN they must complete an action).

column1: Name common access requests that a Conditional Access policy can require MFA for.
column2: Accessing a specific cloud app, a specific network, a specific client application, or registering a new device.

column1: Why should you support more than one MFA authentication method?
column2: So users have a backup option in case their primary method is unavailable.

column1: Which MFA method is preferred for backups?
column2: Call to phone — Azure calls a supplied number and the user approves via the keypad.

column1: What key facts apply to the mobile app OATH verification code method?
column2: The code changes every 30 seconds, works even with limited connectivity, and doesn't work in China on Android devices.

column1: What are FIDO2 security keys?
column2: An unphishable, standards-based passwordless authentication method — typically USB devices, but can also use Bluetooth or NFC.

column1: What does Windows Hello for Business provide?
column2: Strong two-factor authentication on devices that replaces passwords, using a device-tied credential with a biometric or PIN.

column1: What is the easiest approach to get users to register their MFA methods?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID Protection — with a license, configure it to prompt users to register for MFA at their next sign-in.

column1: How can Conditional Access enforce MFA registration for all users?
column2: Apply the policy to a group containing all users, then manually review the group periodically to remove registered users.

column1: Which license is required to configure MFA with Conditional Access in this module's exercise?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 (a 30-day free trial can be used).

column1: What is the portal path to the MFA options page?
column2: Azure portal > Microsoft Entra ID > Security > Multifactor authentication (under Manage).

column1: Where in the portal do you enable or disable app passwords?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID > Security > Multifactor authentication > Additional cloud-based multifactor authentication settings > Service Settings.

column1: What is the purpose of app passwords?
column2: They let users create unique per-app passwords to authenticate to apps that don't support multifactor authentication.

column1: In a Conditional Access policy, which setting enforces MFA?
column2: Under Grant: select Grant access, then Require multifactor authentication, then set Enable policy to On.

column1: In the exercise's guest-user MFA policy, which conditions were configured?
column2: Locations — set Configure to Yes and select Any location.

column1: What happens the next time a user signs into an app protected by a new MFA Conditional Access policy?
column2: The user is prompted to register for MFA and choose a preferred method.

column1: Which authentication method is the only one you cannot disable?
column2: Password.

column1: Which accounts can use security questions for SSPR?
column2: Only non-administrative accounts — the method is available only for SSPR.

column1: How many predefined security questions does Azure provide, and what is the maximum length of custom questions?
column2: 35 predefined questions (translated/localized by browser locale); custom questions max 200 characters.

column1: Who can read or change a user's security questions and answers?
column2: Nobody but the user — answers are stored privately on the user object and can only be answered by the user, during registration.

column1: Which method is available only in SSPR, and what is the recommendation about it?
column2: Email address — avoid email accounts that don't require the user's Microsoft Entra password to access.

column1: Name the three passwordless authentication solutions.
column2: Windows Hello for Business, FIDO2 security keys, and the Microsoft Authenticator app.

column1: What does FIDO stand for?
column2: Fast Identity Online — an open standard for passwordless authentication.

column1: Where can users sign in with FIDO2 security keys?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID-joined or Entra hybrid-joined Windows 10 devices, with SSO to cloud and on-premises resources, and supported browsers.

column1: Which OATH token type does Microsoft Entra ID support for hardware tokens?
column2: OATH-TOTP SHA-1 tokens, of the 30-second or 60-second variety.

column1: What is the limit on secret keys for OATH hardware tokens?
column2: 128 characters (which might not be compatible with all tokens).

column1: In OATH software tokens, who generates the secret key (seed)?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID generates the seed that is input into the app and used to generate each OTP.

column1: Which MFA method is not available to the free/trial Microsoft Entra tier?
column2: Voice call — an automated voice system calls the number and the user confirms via keypad.

column1: On which platforms is the Microsoft Authenticator app available?
column2: Android and iOS.

column1: Which services can use the Microsoft Authenticator app, FIDO2 keys, text messages, and voice calls?
column2: Both Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication and SSPR.

column1: A user enabled for MFA can't authenticate from a legacy non-browser app. What is the fix?
column2: Use an app password — it allows authentication to continue for non-browser apps that don't support MFA.

column1: How does a user sign in using the Microsoft Authenticator app?
column2: Approve a push notification, or enter an OATH verification code from the app after providing username and password.

column1: Where do you monitor authentication method activity for MFA and SSPR adoption?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID > Monitoring > Usage & insights.

column1: What data window is used for the Usage & insights registration statistics?
column2: The last 30 days of audit logs from the combined security info registration and SSPR registration experiences.

column1: Where can you see a specific user's latest registration audit information?
column2: Drill down from the Usage & insights chart by clicking it.

column1: Where can you learn more about SSPR usage in the organization?
column2: The Usage tab on the main Usage & insights view.

column1: Which three passwordless authentication methods provide the most secure sign-in events in Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: Windows Hello for Business, FIDO2 security keys, and the Microsoft Authenticator app.

column1: Which authentication methods can be used as the PRIMARY factor at sign-in?
column2: Password, Windows Hello for Business, and FIDO2 security keys (Microsoft Authenticator app and SMS in preview). OATH tokens and voice calls are secondary only (MFA/SSPR).

column1: Can you disable the password authentication method in Microsoft Entra ID?
column2: No. Passwords cannot be disabled; increase sign-in security by adding multifactor authentication.

column1: You need to support legacy apps that don't support modern authentication with per-user MFA. Which method should you use?
column2: App passwords.

column1: Which verification methods are used ONLY for SSPR (not for MFA)?
column2: Security questions and email address.

column1: What does Microsoft recommend to simplify onboarding for MFA and SSPR?
column2: Enable combined security information registration, and require users to register multiple authentication methods for resiliency.

column1: What is Conditional Access and what does it allow you to control?
column2: Fine-grained control over which users/identities can perform specific activities and access resources, using signals to enforce Zero Trust access decisions.

column1: What are security defaults?
column2: Preconfigured security settings managed by Microsoft, provided at no extra cost, giving organizations a basic level of identity security until they manage their own.

column1: Name three settings enforced by security defaults.
column2: Require all users to register for MFA, require administrators to perform MFA, and block legacy authentication protocols.

column1: What MFA method does security defaults registration use to prevent MFA fatigue attacks?
column2: Number matching—users enter a number displayed on screen into the Microsoft Authenticator app.

column1: What is the grace period for MFA registration when security defaults are enabled?
column2: None—registration is required immediately; users are prompted before accessing any resources.

column1: Which admin roles are required to enable or disable security defaults?
column2: At least a Conditional Access Administrator (Security Administrator also shown in exercises).

column1: What is the portal path to manage security defaults?
column2: Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Overview > Properties > Manage security defaults.

column1: Since when are security defaults potentially already enabled on new tenants?
column2: Tenants created on or after October 22, 2019; security defaults are enabled on all new tenants at creation.

column1: Who should NOT use security defaults?
column2: Organizations already using Conditional Access policies, organizations with Microsoft Entra ID Premium licenses, or those with complex security requirements.

column1: Why is legacy authentication dangerous even with an MFA policy enabled?
column2: Legacy authentication doesn't support MFA, so attackers can use older protocols to bypass multifactor authentication.

column1: Which protocols count as legacy authentication?
column2: Clients not using modern authentication (e.g., Office 2010) and mail protocols like IMAP, SMTP, or POP3.

column1: Does security defaults block Exchange Active Sync basic authentication?
column2: Yes—after security defaults are enabled, all authentication requests made by older protocols are blocked.

column1: How are Conditional Access policies structured?
column2: As if-then statements: if an assignment is met, then apply the access controls. Conditions are called assignments.

column1: What are the three components of a CA policy?
column2: Assignments (users, apps, conditions), Access controls (grant/block), and Session controls.

column1: If no assignment is required and no CA policy is in effect, what is the default behavior?
column2: An access token is issued.

column1: What is report-only mode used for?
column2: Evaluating CA policies before enabling them, to predict affected users without enforcing the policy.

column1: How many emergency access accounts should you create before deploying CA policies?
column2: Two or more, to mitigate accidental administrator lockout from misconfigured policies.

column1: Which license tier is required for Conditional Access?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID Premium P1 (or Microsoft 365 E3 and up); Free and Office 365 subscriptions have no CA.

column1: Which license tier adds risk-based sign-in options to Conditional Access?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID Premium P2, which adds Risky sign-ins, Risky Users, and risk-based options via Identity Protection.

column1: How should block access policies be rolled out?
column2: In phases: communicate changes, start with a small user set, keep administrators excluded, apply to all users only after thorough testing.

column1: What can you use named locations for in CA planning?
column2: To block sign-ins from countries/regions you would never expect, by creating a named location and a policy blocking sign-in from it.

column1: What does Microsoft recommend when first creating a CA policy?
column2: Set Enable policy to Report-only, monitor sign-in logs to verify behavior, then switch it to On.

column1: Which license is required to use sign-in risk-based Conditional Access?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID Premium P2 (Identity Protection sign-in risk detections).

column1: Through which two interfaces can a sign-in risk-based policy be assigned?
column2: Conditional Access itself or Microsoft Entra Identity Protection—organizations should choose one.

column1: Which user action in Conditional Access secures MFA and SSPR registration?
column2: Register security information under Cloud apps or actions > User actions (requires combined registration).

column1: How do you create a policy requiring security info registration only from trusted locations?
column2: User action "Register security information"; Conditions > Locations: include Any location, exclude All trusted locations; Grant control: Block access.

column1: Where are Named locations configured?
column2: Microsoft Entra admin center > Protection > Conditional Access > Named locations.

column1: What two types of named locations can you define?
column2: IP ranges (IPv4 address ranges) or Countries/Regions (with optional inclusion of unknown areas).

column1: Which accounts should always be excluded from CA policies?
column2: Emergency access (break-glass) accounts, service accounts (e.g., Microsoft Entra Connect Sync Account), and service principals.

column1: Why should service accounts be excluded from CA policies?
column2: MFA can't be completed programmatically; consider replacing them with managed identities.

column1: Which grant control requires Intune and blocks non-compliant devices?
column2: Require device to be marked as compliant—Intune sends compliance info to Microsoft Entra ID for CA decisions.

column1: Does the "Require device to be marked as compliant" control block Intune enrollment?
column2: No—new devices can still enroll to Intune even if the control applies to All users and All cloud apps.

column1: What are Terms of Use (TOU) in Conditional Access?
column2: PDF-based terms created in Identity Governance that users must accept before access; consent can be expired or re-attested.

column1: Name two configurations that can block your entire organization if applied to all users and all cloud apps.
column2: Block access, and Require Hybrid Microsoft Entra joined device.

column1: Why is "Require app protection policy" on all users/apps dangerous?
column2: It can block administrators without an Intune app protection policy client app from accessing portals like Intune and Azure.

column1: Which two tools should be used to validate CA policies before enabling?
column2: Conditional Access report-only mode and the What If tool.

column1: Which roles can review sign-in events for CA troubleshooting?
column2: Security Administrator or Global Reader.

column1: Where do you find which CA policies applied to a failed sign-in?
column2: Identity > Monitoring and Health > Sign-ins > select the event > Conditional Access tab.

column1: Which filters help investigate a specific sign-in failure?
column2: Correlation ID, Conditional access (filtered to failures), Username, and Date.

column1: What information should be provided when opening a support incident for a sign-in failure?
column2: The request ID and the time and date from the sign-in event.

column1: In the CA policy details view of a sign-in event, what does each side show?
column2: Left side: details collected at sign-in; right side: whether those details satisfy the applied policies' requirements.

column1: What architecture does Conditional Access App Control use?
column2: Reverse proxy architecture, integrated with Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, routing users to Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.

column1: Where are access and session policies for Conditional Access App Control configured?
column2: In the Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps portal.

column1: Name three things Conditional Access App Control can do in a session.
column2: Prevent data exfiltration (block download/copy/print), protect on download via Azure Information Protection labels, block upload of unlabeled files, and monitor risky user sessions.

column1: What must iOS and Android devices do before you can require approved client apps for them?
column2: They must first register in Microsoft Entra ID.

column1: What are app protection policies (APP)?
