column2: No sign-in within 30 days (last sign-in date is shown), and peer outlier — the user lacks the same access as peers, based on average distance in the reporting structure.

column1: What happens when "Take recommendations" is used in an access review?
column2: At the end of the review, the system automatically applies the recommendations for users that reviewers failed to respond to.

column1: Does the "no sign-in within 30 days" recommendation consider only interactive sign-ins?
column2: No — it applies to both interactive and non-interactive sign-ins.

column1: Through which actions can external identities be granted access to company resources?
column2: Added to a group, invited to Teams, assigned to an enterprise application or access package, or assigned a privileged role in Microsoft Entra ID or an Azure subscription.

column1: Which options define when a recurring access review series ends?
column2: Never, a specific end date, or a set number of occurrences.

column1: When updating a running recurring review, what is the difference between applying changes to Current vs. Series?
column2: Current changes only the active review instance; Series applies changes to all future recurrences (e.g., replace a reviewer who left the organization).

column1: Where do reviewers complete access reviews with the Access Review Agent, and what does it provide?
column2: In Microsoft Teams via natural-language conversation; it analyzes active reviews, generates approve/deny recommendations with a justification summary, and lets reviewers ask questions before deciding.

column1: Which signals does the Access Review Agent use for its recommendations?
column2: User inactivity; user-to-group affiliation; account enabled (accountEnabled); employment status (employeeLeaveDateTime); lifecycle workflow history (mover workflow in past 30 days); decisions from previous reviews; access request history.

column1: Which user property does the Access Review Agent use to detect that a user's employment ended?
column2: employeeLeaveDateTime.

column1: What are the license prerequisites for the Access Review Agent?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID Governance or Microsoft Entra Suite licenses, plus onboarding to Security Copilot with at least one security compute unit (SCU).

column1: Which roles must admins have to set up and manage the Access Review Agent?
column2: Identity Governance Administrator, Lifecycle Workflows Administrator, and Security Copilot Contributor.

column1: What must reviewers have to use the Access Review Agent?
column2: Access to Microsoft Teams, an active access review assigned, and the Security Copilot Contributor role.

column1: Once started, can an Access Review Agent run be stopped or paused?
column2: No — agents can't be stopped or paused once started; a run may take a few minutes. It's recommended to run the agent from the Microsoft Entra admin center.

column1: How do you enable the Access Review Agent for an existing access review?
column2: ID Governance > Access reviews > select the review > Settings under Manage (one-time) or Series (recurring) > Advanced Settings > check "Access Review Agent (Preview)" > Save.

column1: What is Privileged Identity Management (PIM)?
column2: A service in Microsoft Entra ID for managing, controlling, and monitoring access to privileged resources such as Microsoft Entra ID, Azure, Microsoft 365, and Intune.

column1: Which license is required to use PIM?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID Premium P2.

column1: You need just-in-time privileged access with approval-based role activation. Which feature should you use?
column2: Privileged Identity Management (PIM).

column1: List key features of PIM.
column2: Just-in-time access, time-bound access with start/end dates, approval to activate roles, MFA enforcement for activation, justification on activation, notifications, access reviews, and audit history download.

column1: Who can bring Azure resources under PIM management during discovery?
column2: Only owners of subscriptions and management groups.

column1: A Global Administrator wants to discover all Azure subscriptions for PIM but lacks access. What should they do?
column2: Elevate access to manage all Azure subscriptions in the directory.

column1: What is the principle of least privilege in the context of Microsoft Entra roles?
column2: Assign administrators the least powerful, most specific roles needed instead of Global Administrator, and remove unnecessary privileged assignments.

column1: Which PIM feature can automate removing users from unnecessary Microsoft Entra roles?
column2: Access reviews in PIM (set reviewers to "Members (self)" and require reason on approval).

column1: What should you do if privileged accounts don't have emails linked for access reviews?
column2: Populate the secondary email field on those accounts.

column1: Which two Microsoft Entra roles does Microsoft recommend managing with PIM first?
column2: Global Administrator and Security Administrator.

column1: Which roles should always be protected with PIM for less-critical Azure subscriptions?
column2: Owner and User Access Administrator roles.

column1: How should service accounts be treated in PIM for Azure resources?
column2: Exactly the same as regular user accounts (PIM supports time-bound service accounts).

column1: When should you assign a role to a group instead of individual users?
column2: When many users are assigned to a role, or when you want to delegate assigning the role.

column1: Who can manage membership of a Microsoft Entra role-assignable group?
column2: Only the Privileged Role Administrator, the Global Administrator, and the group owners.

column1: When a role-assignable group is brought under PIM management, what is it called?
column2: A privileged access group.

column1: In PIM, when a group member activates a role-assignable group, what is activated?
column2: Only the user's group membership — the group itself is not activated.

column1: What is the difference between eligible and permanently active role assignments?
column2: Eligible roles require an action (MFA, justification, approval) to activate; permanently active roles are always assigned with no activation needed.

column1: How many permanently active Global Administrator assignments does Microsoft recommend?
column2: Zero, except for the two break-glass emergency access accounts.

column1: What factors should you consider when deciding eligible vs. permanent role assignment?
column2: Frequency of elevation (one-time need vs. day-to-day job) and organization-specific cases (distant teams, high-ranking executives).

column1: What does Microsoft recommend for users with permanent role assignments?
column2: Set up recurring access reviews for them.

column1: Who receives email notifications when an eligible user activates a role (if notification is enabled)?
column2: Global Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator, and Security Administrator.

column1: What is the default set of approvers for a PIM role requiring approval?
column2: All users who are Privileged Role Administrators (permanent or eligible).

column1: If a user is both eligible for a role and an approver of that role, can they approve their own activation?
column2: No, they cannot approve themselves.

column1: What is the purpose of the incident ticket setting in PIM?
column2: Requires the user to record an incident ticket number at activation, tying activations to internal incident numbers.

column1: Which Microsoft Entra roles are most commonly configured with approval required?
column2: Global Administrator, User Administrator, Exchange Administrator, Security Administrator, and Password Administrator.

column1: What is the difference between "Permanent admin" and "Active admin" in PIM settings?
column2: Permanent admin applies to Microsoft Entra roles (never activate); Active admin applies to Azure resources and can have an expiration time set.

column1: What expiration options are available for active and eligible Azure role assignments?
column2: 15 days, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, 1 year, or permanently active/eligible.

column1: Is there a limit to the number of Azure resources you can manage with PIM?
column2: No, there is no limit, though Microsoft recommends starting with the most critical production resources.

column1: When you manage a management group or subscription in PIM, what else can you manage?
column2: Its child resources.

column1: You add a new child Azure resource to a PIM-managed management group. How do you bring it under PIM management?
column2: Search for it in PIM and add it.

column1: Which portal path do you use to discover Azure resources in PIM?
column2: Microsoft Entra admin center > Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management > Azure resources > Discover resources.

column1: What is the difference between Eligible and Active assignment types in PIM?
column2: Eligible requires an action (MFA, justification, or approval) to use the role; Active grants the privileges always, with no action required.

column1: Where does a user go to activate an eligible Microsoft Entra role?
column2: Privileged Identity Management > My roles > select the role > Activate.

column1: How often must a user perform MFA verification when activating roles in a session?
column2: Only once per session.

column1: Which roles can PIM manage for Azure resources?
column2: Built-in Azure resource roles and custom roles, including Owner, User Access Administrator, Contributor, Security Admin, and Security Manager.

column1: For which roles can the scope of permissions be restricted in a PIM assignment?
column2: Certain roles can be scoped to a single administrative unit, service principal, or application.

column1: If multiple approvers are configured for a PIM role, how many approvals are needed?
column2: Only one — approval completes as soon as one approver approves or denies; you cannot require approval from at least two users.

column1: What is a privileged access group used for?
column2: Assigning eligibility for membership or ownership of a role-assignable group, giving workload-specific administrators quick access to multiple roles with a single just-in-time request.

column1: How can you enforce different activation policies for employees vs. B2B partner guests?
column2: Create two different privileged access groups with their own policies (less strict for employees, stricter with approval workflow for partners).

column1: Which PIM view shows all activity associated with a privileged access group?
column2: Resource audit (under Groups > select group > Activity > Resource audit).

column1: Which PIM view shows your personal role activity for a privileged access group?
column2: My audit (under Groups > select group > Activity > My audit).

column1: Which role assignments are not shown in PIM audit history for privileged access groups?
column2: Role assignments authorized by a service provider using Azure delegated resource management.

column1: What are emergency access (break-glass) accounts?
column2: Highly privileged, cloud-only accounts not assigned to specific individuals, used only when normal administrative accounts cannot be used.

column1: How many emergency access accounts should an organization create?
column2: Two or more.

column1: What type of accounts should emergency access accounts be?
column2: Cloud-only accounts using the .onmicrosoft.com domain, not federated or synchronized from on-premises.

column1: What role assignment should emergency access accounts have?
column2: Permanent Global Administrator role assignment.

column1: Why should at least one emergency access account be excluded from phone-based MFA and Conditional Access policies?
column2: So a policy or unavailable MFA mechanism cannot block access during an emergency; a different authentication mechanism should be configured instead.

column1: Which tool can monitor sign-in logs of break-glass accounts and trigger alerts?
column2: Azure Log Analytics (email and SMS alerts to admins on break-glass sign-ins).

column1: How often should emergency access accounts be validated?
column2: At least every 90 days, and after key changes such as IT staff changes or changes to Microsoft Entra subscriptions.

column1: Name scenarios where an emergency access account is needed.
column2: Federation/identity-provider outage, MFA service or device unavailability, last Global Administrator leaving the organization, and unforeseen circumstances like natural disasters.

column1: What should you verify about MFA registration on emergency access accounts?
column2: That users haven't registered MFA or SSPR to any individual user's device or personal details, and that any registered device is accessible to all administrators with at least two network paths that don't share a common failure mode.

column1: Which three log types make up the "Activity" component of the Microsoft Entra ID reporting architecture?
column2: Sign-ins, Audit logs, and Provisioning logs.

column1: What is a risky sign-in?
column2: An indicator for a sign-in attempt by someone who isn't the legitimate owner of a user account.

column1: What is a risky user?
column2: An indicator that a user account might have been compromised.

column1: Which built-in roles can access sign-in and risk reporting data?
column2: Security Administrator, Security Reader, Global Reader, and Report Reader.

column1: Can non-admin users access sign-in data?
column2: Yes — any user (non-admin) can access their own sign-ins.

column1: Which license is required to access the sign-in activity report?
column2: None specifically — the sign-in activity report is available in all editions of Microsoft Entra ID (also via Microsoft Graph API).

column1: How long does it take for sign-in records to appear in the portal?
column2: Up to two hours.

column1: You need to view service-to-service (non-interactive) authentication in the Sign-ins report. What should you tell the admin?
column2: Not possible — the sign-ins report only displays interactive sign-ins; non-interactive sign-ins are not displayed.

column1: You need to export sign-in logs to work with data outside the Azure portal. Which formats and limits apply?
column2: Download as CSV or JSON, up to the most recent 250,000 records (constrained by report retention policies).

column1: In sign-in logs, what does Conditional Access status "Failure" mean?
column2: The sign-in satisfied the user and application condition of at least one CA policy, and grant controls were not satisfied or set to block access.

column1: In sign-in logs, what does Conditional Access status "Not applied" mean?
column2: No policy applied to the user and application during the sign-in.

column1: Which sign-in log filter shows whether a user signed in via browser, mobile app/desktop client, or Exchange ActiveSync?
column2: The Client app filter.

column1: Why might an IP address map to a wrong physical location in Microsoft Entra reports?
column2: Location conversion is best effort; mobile providers and VPNs issue IP addresses from central pools far from the client device.

column1: You need an application-centric view of sign-in data for your top three applications. Where do you look?
column2: Enterprise applications > Overview > last 30 days report (app-usage graphs, weekly aggregation, default 30 days).

column1: Where is the only place to get a full view of Microsoft 365 activity logs?
column2: The Microsoft 365 admin center (also programmatically via Office 365 Management APIs).

column1: What is the default time period for the Identity Protection user sign-in graph?
column2: 30 days (weekly aggregations of sign-ins).

column1: Where do you access the Microsoft Entra audit logs report?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID > Monitoring > Audit logs.

column1: What does an audit log default list view show?
column2: Date/time, service that logged it, category and activity name (what), status (success/failure), target, and initiator/actor (who).

column1: Which audit log category is preselected when viewing audit logs from the Users tab?
column2: UserManagement.

column1: Which audit log category is preselected when viewing audit logs from the Groups tab?
column2: GroupManagement.

column1: Which filter is preselected when viewing audit logs from Enterprise applications?
column2: Enterprise applications as the Application Type.

column1: What are the possible values of the audit log Status filter?
column2: All, Success, Failure.

column1: Which audit log filters are case-sensitive?
column2: Target and Initiated by (Actor) — both name and UPN are case-sensitive.

column1: What are the Date range filter options for audit logs?
column2: 7 days, 24 hours, or Custom (with configurable start and end time).

column1: How can you retrieve the full list of audit activities programmatically?
column2: Via the Graph API: graph.windows.net/<tenantdomain>/activities/auditActivityTypesV2?api-version=beta

column1: What is Microsoft Sentinel?
column2: A scalable, cloud-native SIEM and SOAR solution that collects, detects, investigates, and responds to threats across the enterprise.

column1: Which license is required to ingest sign-in logs into Microsoft Sentinel?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2.

column1: Which licenses are sufficient to ingest non-sign-in Microsoft Entra log types into Sentinel?
column2: Any Microsoft Entra ID license (Free/O365/P1/P2).

column1: Which two roles must a user have to connect Microsoft Entra logs to Microsoft Sentinel?
column2: Microsoft Sentinel Contributor (on the workspace) and Security Administrator (on the tenant streaming the logs).

column1: Which log types can be streamed via the Microsoft Sentinel Microsoft Entra ID connector?
column2: Sign-in logs and audit logs.

column1: What is the Microsoft recommended approach for integrating Azure with SIEM tools?
column2: Route data via Azure Monitor to Azure Event Hubs, where SIEM connectors consume the data.

column1: Which tool should a Splunk customer use for SIEM integration?
column2: The Azure Monitor Add-On for Splunk (migrate away from AzLog).

column1: Which components should IBM QRadar customers use for Azure integration?
column2: Microsoft Azure DSM and Microsoft Azure Event Hubs Protocol (from the IBM support website).

column1: Which Microsoft Entra log type was directly integrated with AzLog but not yet available in Azure Monitor?
column2: Microsoft Entra logs.

column1: What is AzLog?
column2: The Azure Log Integration tool, used to consolidate, translate, and forward logs from Azure services to a SIEM tool before Azure Monitor existed.

column1: Which license is required to access the usage and insights report?
column2: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2.

column1: Which roles can access the usage and insights report?
column2: Security Administrator, Security Reader, or Report Reader.

column1: Where do you find the usage and insights report?
column2: Azure portal > Microsoft Entra ID > Enterprise applications > Activity > Usage and insights.

column1: What can you sort by in the usage and insights report?
column2: Number of successful sign-ins, failed sign-ins, and success rate.

column1: What is the identity secure score?
column2: A percentage indicating how aligned your identity security is with Microsoft's best practice recommendations.

column1: Which license is required for identity secure score?
column2: None — it's available in all editions of Microsoft Entra ID.

column1: What is the portal path to access the identity secure score?
column2: Azure portal > Microsoft Entra ID > Security > Identity Secure Score.

column1: What does the identity secure score dashboard's comparison graph show?
column2: How your score compares to other tenants in the same industry and of similar size.

column1: How are identity secure score controls scored?
column2: Two ways — binary (100% if configured per recommendation) or as a percentage of total configuration (partial credit, e.g., MFA for some users).

column1: Besides configuring security features, what other task type improves your secure score?
column2: Security-related tasks, like reading reports.
